cases.title: Identical after-turn capture replayed under the same idempotency key

when.action: The host redelivers a byte-identical after-turn capture request after a transport timeout.

expect.rationale: A redelivered identical request returns the first recorded result. No second candidate observation is produced and no additional effect is created.

cases.title: Divergent after-turn capture reusing a spent idempotency key

when.action: The host reuses a spent idempotency key while sending a different capture payload.

expect.rationale: Reusing a key for a different request is a caller defect, not a transient fault. Retrying the identical request fails identically, so the failure is non-retryable.

cases.title: Effecting hook submitted with no idempotency key

when.action: The host omits the idempotency key on a hook that can produce an effect.

expect.rationale: The frozen contract makes the idempotency key required on effecting operations. Accepting the call would leave duplicate suppression undefined for the whole run.

cases.title: Duplicate tool-result persistence for one tool call

when.action: The host persists the same oversized tool result twice, both times by reference to the same content handle.

expect.rationale: The reference handle and idempotency key together identify one persistence effect. The second call returns the first handle rather than creating a second record.

cases.title: Duplicate run-local tool approval for an already-decided approval

when.action: The host re-requests a run-local tool approval that a human operator has already denied within the same turn.

expect.rationale: A decided run-local approval is replayed with its recorded decision, so re-asking cannot re-open a denial or produce a second prompt the operator could tire of and accept. The decision stays run-local: it is never a Core governance decision, creates no Core governance audit entry and grants no capability.

cases.title: After-turn capture arrives before the turn it belongs to opened

when.action: A capture callback for turn ordinal 3 at sequence 4 is delivered while the run has only opened turn ordinals 0 through 1.

expect.rationale: A capture for an unopened turn has no lifecycle position to attach to. Buffering it would let the SPI hold run state, which it does not own.

cases.title: Stale recall callback delivered after a newer turn opened

when.action: A delayed before-turn recall for sequence 2 is redelivered after sequence 5 has already been served.

expect.rationale: A recall is a read with no effect, so a stale delivery is dropped rather than refused. It is still audited so a reordering host can be diagnosed.

cases.title: Host-local compaction notification interleaved between recall and capture

when.action: The host compacts its own transcript midway through an open turn and notifies the provider.

expect.rationale: Compaction is host and run-state owned. The provider acknowledges the host-local lifecycle notification and drops it: Core writes no run-state record and no audit entry, and Core exposes no compaction or run-state operation, so ordering relative to the turn is not Core's concern.

cases.title: Effecting hook delivered after its own turn reached a terminal state

when.action: A capture for turn ordinal 7 arrives after `turn.complete` closed that turn.

expect.rationale: Turn completion is terminal for the identified turn, so a late effect for that turn fails closed. It is not run completion: the Workflow Run stays open and a later turn remains possible, which `SPI-V-039` asserts.

cases.title: Recall attempted without an authenticated principal

when.action: The host presents a caller claim with no authenticated session behind it.

expect.rationale: Host-supplied identity is a claim. Without validation against an authenticated session or trusted local configuration it grants nothing.

cases.title: Recall targets a workspace the principal was never granted

when.action: The host rebinds the run to a second workspace mid-session and recalls from it.

expect.rationale: Workspace binding is fixed for the run. Cross-workspace recall is denied before any candidate is ranked, so nothing unauthorised is ever scored.

cases.title: Capture requested without the write capability

when.action: A read-only adapter invokes after-turn capture.

expect.rationale: The effective capability set is the intersection of what the server supports and what the principal was granted. A hook cannot draw on anything outside it.

cases.title: Search submitted with a purpose outside the granted allowlist

when.action: The host declares a purpose that no session grant or allowlist entry covers.

expect.rationale: Purpose is validated before retrieval runs. Deferring the check until after ranking would already have read content the purpose did not license.

cases.title: Recalled content instructs the adapter to widen its capabilities

when.action: Recalled evidence text contains an embedded instruction to grant governed mutation, and the host forwards it as a capability request.

expect.rationale: Recalled content, tool arguments and model output are untrusted data. They can never expand the granted set, so the injection has no privileged path to act on.

cases.title: Governed mutation attempted directly instead of through the approval boundary

when.action: The adapter asks capture to write a governed record rather than a candidate observation.

expect.rationale: Capture produces candidate observations only. Promotion to governed knowledge is a separate application-contract governance path taken by a validated principal holding `knowledge.govern`, with its own approval and audit. A run-local host approval cannot stand in for it, and a turn ending never promotes anything.

cases.title: Search requested while the workspace lease is held elsewhere

when.action: Another writer holds the workspace service lease when the hook is invoked.

expect.rationale: The SPI reuses the frozen error catalogue rather than minting a host-specific code, so an adapter's backoff behaviour matches every other client of the same workspace.

cases.title: Turn cancellation accepted while a recall is in flight

when.action: The operator cancels the turn while a before-turn recall is still executing and a Core durable job the turn started is outstanding.

expect.rationale: Cancellation is cooperative and turn-scoped. The in-flight recall's result is discarded rather than delivered, and the outstanding Core job handle is returned unchanged so the host can act on it separately. `turn.cancel` never composes `job.cancel`, and cancelling provider turn state needs no `job.control`.

cases.title: Cancellation of an already-cancelled turn

when.action: A second cancellation is issued for a turn already in a cancelled state.

expect.rationale: A state-based refusal of a control call is a successful idempotent result carrying the unchanged handle, not a `conflict` error, matching the frozen `JobCancellationDisposition` semantics. The replay composes no Core job control either.

cases.title: Turn cancellation races an after-turn capture that has already taken effect

when.action: Cancellation arrives after a capture committed its candidate observation but before the host observed the response.

expect.rationale: Cancellation stops future work; it never rewinds a completed effect. The already-recorded candidate keeps its audit reference and remains discoverable, and any Core durable job the turn started keeps running until the host issues its own `job.cancel`.

cases.title: Turn cancellation asked to cancel the outstanding Core durable job

when.action: The adapter asks `turn.cancel` to also cancel the Core durable job the turn started, as one composed call.

expect.rationale: Turn cancellation cancels provider turn state only. Composing `job.cancel` implicitly would stop durable Core work on the authority of a host-local control action. The outstanding job handles are returned instead, and the host makes a separate, explicitly authorized and idempotent application-contract `job.cancel` call. Holding `job.control` does not change this: the composition is what is refused, not the capability.

cases.title: Recall exceeds the deadline the host declared

when.action: The recall is still ranking when the declared deadline elapses.

expect.rationale: A recall has no effect to unwind, so the identical request may be retried. The host receives no partial ranking it could mistake for a complete one.

cases.title: Effecting hook exceeds its deadline mid-flight

when.action: The capture deadline elapses while the effect is uncertain from the host's point of view.

expect.rationale: The deadline leaves no partial canonical effect. The retained idempotency key makes the retry safe: it either replays the recorded result or performs the effect once.

cases.title: Nested hook declares a deadline longer than its parent

when.action: A search nested inside a recall with 2000 ms remaining declares a 30000 ms deadline.

expect.rationale: Deadlines shrink monotonically down a call chain. A child that could outlive its parent would let a cancelled turn keep consuming workspace resources.

cases.title: Hook submitted with no deadline at all

when.action: The adapter omits `deadline_ms` and relies on an implicit server default.

expect.rationale: An unbounded hook call has no cancellation story. Requiring an explicit deadline keeps turn latency a property the host states rather than one it discovers.

cases.title: Hook invoked before negotiation completed

when.action: The adapter calls a lifecycle hook without first completing `spi.negotiate`.

expect.rationale: Without negotiation neither side knows the agreed SPI version or effective capability set, so any subsequent hook would be interpreting fields on an unagreed contract.

cases.title: Adapter declares a newer compatible minor SPI version

when.action: The adapter declares SPI 1.2.0 against a server supporting 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 and sends unknown optional fields.

expect.rationale: The server selects 1.1.0 and ignores the unknown optional fields. An additive minor difference must not present as a production break.

cases.title: Adapter declares an unsupported major SPI version

when.action: The adapter declares SPI 2.0.0 against a server that supports only the 1.x line.

expect.rationale: A major difference is a breaking wire change. Negotiating down would silently reinterpret fields whose meaning changed.

cases.title: Adapter requires a capability version the server does not implement

when.action: The adapter marks `memory.write@9.0` as required during negotiation.

expect.rationale: Servers reject unknown required capability versions rather than proceeding degraded, so the adapter fails at handshake instead of part-way through a turn.

cases.title: Negotiation succeeds with a deprecated but supported capability

when.action: The adapter negotiates against a capability carrying deprecation metadata and a stated removal version.

expect.rationale: Deprecation is reported in the handshake, not discovered at removal. The adapter keeps working and has a named version to migrate before.

cases.title: Workspace format requires migration before any hook can run

when.action: Negotiation targets a workspace whose format predates the server's minimum supported version.

expect.rationale: The SPI never migrates a workspace as a side effect of a handshake. Migration is an explicit operator action with its own gate.

cases.title: Retry of a failed capture reuses the original idempotency key

when.action: The host retries the failed `capture.after_turn` hook after a `deadline_exceeded`, presenting the original key.

expect.rationale: `turn.retry` re-drives the failed provider hook under the original key and the frozen retry classification. The retained key is what makes a retryable failure safe to retry, and server state decides whether the recorded result is replayed or the effect is performed once. No Core `job.retry` is composed.

cases.title: Retry attempted on a non-retryable authorization denial

when.action: The host retries a hook that previously failed with `authorization_denied`.

expect.rationale: The identical request fails identically. Retry must not be a way to grind against an authorization boundary.

cases.title: Adapter presents an unrecognised retry class

when.action: A future server returns a retry class the adapter build does not know, and the adapter must decide whether to retry.

expect.rationale: An unrecognised retry class is preserved but never inferred to be retryable. Guessing would turn an open vocabulary into an accidental retry storm.

cases.title: Adapter requires a patch to host source to satisfy the SPI

when.action: A candidate hook signature can only be satisfied by editing the agent host's own source tree.

expect.rationale: Hosts are adapters. A hook that cannot be implemented from a host's public extension surface is a design defect in the SPI, not a licence to fork the host.

cases.title: Adapter attempts to read the workspace database directly

when.action: The adapter bypasses the application boundary and opens the workspace store itself.

expect.rationale: Direct storage access bypasses ACL enforcement, the lease and audit at once. The SPI has no path that reaches storage other than the application contract.

cases.title: Host asks Core to hold run state between turns

when.action: The host asks Core to store the task graph and token budget so the host can drop them.

expect.rationale: Run state is owned by the Workflow Runtime or a shared Run State service. Core exposes no operation that creates, reads, lists, cancels or replays workflow-run state, so there is no hook that could accept the task graph or token budget.

cases.title: Compaction summary offered as canonical knowledge

when.action: After a host-local compaction the adapter submits the lossy summary through capture, for promotion into governed knowledge.

expect.rationale: Compression is lossy and unreviewed. A compaction summary may enter Core only through capture, as a candidate observation carrying bounded provenance that a host-local compaction occurred — never as canonical truth, and never through `context.compact`, which persists nothing in Core.

cases.title: Oversized tool result submitted inline instead of by reference

when.action: The adapter inlines a tool result above the declared byte ceiling rather than passing a content reference.

expect.rationale: Oversized payloads move by reference so the hook stays bounded. Resending the identical inline payload fails identically, so the failure is non-retryable.

cases.title: A later turn opens in a run whose earlier turn already completed

when.action: Turn ordinal 7 completed; the host opens turn ordinal 8 in the same run and calls before-turn recall.

expect.rationale: Turn completion is terminal for one turn, not for the run. A Workflow Run may contain many turns or task nodes, so a later turn must remain possible. Refusing it would make `turn.complete` behave as run completion, a boundary the SPI does not own.

cases.title: Turn retry asked to retry the outstanding Core durable job

when.action: The adapter asks `turn.retry` to also retry the Core durable job the failed hook had started, as one composed call.

expect.rationale: `turn.retry` resumes the provider hook only. A Core durable job retry is a separate application operation with its own authorization and its own idempotency key; composing it implicitly would re-drive durable Core work on the authority of a host-local recovery action. Holding `job.control` does not change this.

cases.title: Run-local tool approval offered as authority for a governed mutation

when.action: The host presents a run-local tool approval a human granted during the turn as the authority for a governed mutation.

expect.rationale: A host or runtime tool approval is run-local. It is not a Core governance decision, records no Core governance audit entry and cannot grant `knowledge.govern`. A Core governance escalation is a separate application-contract path taken by a validated principal. Core audits the denied authorization attempt; the run-local approval itself is never recorded as a decision.

cases.title: Adapter injects host identity into the frozen request envelope

when.action: The adapter adds agent, session, run and turn-ordinal fields to `RequestMetadata` on the nested Core application call.

expect.rationale: The frozen `RequestMetadata` sets `unevaluatedProperties: false` and defines no agent, session, run or turn field, so the injection is a malformed envelope. Host identifiers are SPI-local provenance carried by the host-provider wrapper; caller and workspace authority stay Core-validated, and no agent, session, run or turn value ever widens authority.
